items.title: 5 smartwatches you should buy instead of the Moto Watch Ultra
items.summary: There are a lot of great options out there.
items.body: The Moto Watch Ultra is Motorola’s latest smartwatch, featuring a unique blend of features for the price. The singular variant costs $350 and includes LTE eSIM support, Wear OS 6, a 1.5-inch pOLED display, and Polar’s health and fitness tracking algorithms. That’s a fabulous combination in itself, but Motorola has cut corners on the processor and is only offering two OS upgrades. Thankfully, there’s no shortage of good Wear OS smartwatch options in the market. From Google to Samsung, there are plenty of great alternatives you should consider first. So, before settling on the Moto Watch Ultra, consider these five other alternatives.

items.title: I used Immich for years, but this self-hosted Google Photos alternative is even better
items.summary: Noodle Gallery takes everything I love about Immich and adds smarter ways to share, organize, and manage family photos.
items.body: I’ve had Immich running on my home server for the past three years. It’s a self-hosting essential for me as I try to offload as much of my backups and services from the cloud as possible. It’s where I keep the photos from my SLR, where my phone backs up photos automatically, and where I can search through years of images without handing everything over to Google. For a self-hosted alternative to Google Photos , there’s little doubt that Immich is the go-to for most. But as good as Immich is, as an enthusiast, I was bound to run into limitations. Immich is great at managing individual photo libraries, but it isn’t always great at managing a family’s photo library. If you’re trying to share a portion of your library, Immich makes it extremely hard. And you can absolutely forget about sharing certain aspects of the library, like metadata.

items.title: Charlie Puth Cancels Australian and New Zealand Arena Dates
items.summary: No reason for the cancellation has been announced.
items.body: Charlie Puth has cancelled his upcoming Australian and New Zealand tour, scrapping a number of November arena dates first announced in April. The six-date arena run was due to begin at Auckland’s Spark Arena in early November before heading to Australia for concerts in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth. According to an email sent to ticket holders, the shows will no longer proceed and all tickets will be automatically refunded to the original payment method. Fans do not need to take any action to receive their refunds. Ticketing outlets have also listed the concerts as canceled and removed tickets from sale. No reason for the cancellation has been announced, and Puth had not publicly addressed the decision at press time. It is not yet known whether replacement dates will be scheduled. Announced in April, the regional run was set to mark Puth’s first Australian visit since 2023. The singer had promised fans an “unforgettable live experience” featuring a “world-class band.” “I feel like I’ve worked and waited my entire career to put this sort of live show on for you all,” Puth said when announcing the dates. items.title: Gemini’s rough patch with smart home controls has spread to Android Auto
items.summary: One Gemini smart home bug gets fixed, another pops up.
items.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Some Android Auto users say Gemini has suddenly stopped controlling their smart home devices. The issue follows recent Gemini smart home control problems on Wear OS, which Google said it had fixed. It’s not clear what’s causing the Android Auto problem — we’ve reached out to Google for comment. Gemini has had a rough couple of weeks with smart home controls. Wear OS users recently reported that Gemini would claim it had controlled lights, AC units, and other devices when nothing actually happened , before Google said that the issue had been fixed . It isn’t clear if it’s related, but some Android Auto users are now finding that Gemini suddenly refuses to control their smart home devices, even though those same commands worked previously. In a post on the r/AndroidAuto subreddit earlier today, one user says that Gemini has stopped executing commands such as turning on the AC. Instead, it now responds that it “cannot control smart home devices through Google Maps while driving.” The poster says the feature had been working for months before this change.

The research is part of NASA’s exploration of the extreme universe to better understand how the cosmos works. “We’ve never before seen clear indications of wind plasma falling onto a compact object,” said Roi Rahin, a researcher at UMBC (University of Maryland, Baltimore County) and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “We can now test our understanding of these processes in much greater detail.” A paper describing the findings published Friday in the journal Science Advances. The target system is BP Crucis, a high-mass X-ray binary located about 13,000 light-years away in the southern constellation Crux. items.title: Android 17 QPR1 fixes a major headache for enthusiasts
items.summary: No more turning developer options off to check your bank account.
items.body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Pixel phones now. The update no longer allows third-party apps to see whether you have developer settings or USB debugging active. This should make life easier for anyone who tinkers with Android’s more advanced settings. Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out now to Pixel phones going back to the Pixel 6. The update brings a number of changes, including UI tweaks, the option to include photo location metadata in images shared through Android’s media picker, and more. As spotted by a user on X, QPR1 also quietly fixes an issue that’s been a thorn in the side of Android enthusiasts for years. As developer Sameera Wijerahna points out in a post on X , Android 17 QPR1 no longer lets third-party apps see the state of developer options or debugging settings. This could be a big deal for developers or anyone else who likes to tinker with their Android devices — prior to the change, some apps wouldn’t open on devices with certain settings active.

items.body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s new Security State libraries let apps check the security status of individual Android components instead of relying only on the overall security patch level. items.title: Your smartwatch is probably good enough, and the market knows it
items.summary: The smartwatch upgrade itch isn't quite as itchy as it once was.
items.body: TL;DR Global smartwatch shipments fell 4% year over year in Q2 2026, as people held onto their existing watches for longer. Huawei led global shipments, while Apple posted the fastest growth among the top five smartwatch brands. Counterpoint expects just 1% shipment growth in 2026, but AI and advanced health features could give users more reason to upgrade. Buying a new smartwatch has become difficult. If the one on your wrist still tracks your workouts, shows your notifications, and gets you through the day, why spend another few hundred dollars on a new one? Plenty of people are asking themselves the same question. New data from Counterpoint Research shows that global smartwatch shipments fell 4% year over year in Q2 2026. That’s notable because there are more choices than ever, ranging from cheap watches that cover the basics to expensive models loaded with health and fitness features. But having more watches to choose from doesn’t necessarily mean people want to replace the ones they already own.

items.title: Survey reveals where most of you draw the line when it comes to AI
items.summary: Our reader poll put LLM trust to the test by asking whether you'd hand an agent full access to your computer.
items.body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority LLMs have only been on the scene for a few years, but for better or worse, they’ve long since escaped the chat window. Instead of just answering questions or rewriting your emails, the next wave of AI agents wants to do most of the clicking for you, but this generally requires getting its hands on much more of your computer. We can probably all agree that this could save you a lot of tedious work, but it also means handing a somewhat unpredictable machine the digital equivalent of your house keys. We wanted to know if you were cool with that. That trade-off came into focus when we tried OpenClaw earlier this year, an open-source tool that effectively lets an LLM work directly with your computer and connected services. We found it could be impressively capable when given that freedom, but we also saw how prompt injection could potentially turn the same access against you . In our OpenClaw coverage, we ran a reader poll to ask you a simple question: Would you give an LLM full access to your computer? Late last year, Google introduced an all-new attempt at making Gemini a lot more useful for everyday life. Called CC, it was a new AI agent designed to give you a daily briefing and help you follow up on tasks by tracking information found within your Gmail, Calendar, and Drive. The Google Labs experiment evolved into Gemini’s Daily Brief , and Google is now taking the original CC concept and expanding its horizon. items.body: Credit: NASA NASA has selected SpaceX to provide launch services for the agency’s StarBurst mission, a small satellite designed to investigate neutron star mergers and the origins of short gamma-ray bursts. StarBurst will launch aboard a Bandwagon rideshare mission on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida no earlier than 2028. The selection is a firm-fixed-price task order under NASA’s VADR (Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare) launch services contract. This indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract allows NASA to acquire launch services during a 10-year ordering period, with a maximum total value of $1 billion across all contracts. The StarBurst mission is designed to observe the entire portion of the sky not blocked by Earth to search for brief, powerful explosions called gamma-ray bursts. The satellite will focus on detecting the initial high-energy emission from short gamma-ray bursts, which occur when dense stellar remnants called neutron stars merge. items.title: Claude can now automatically choose which mode is best for you
items.summary: Chat vs. Cowork: Claude is asking you to make one less decision before it gets to work.
items.body: Credit: Mitja Rutnik / Android Authority TL;DR Anthropic is eliminating a major source of friction in its chat interface. Claude can now automatically choose between Chat and Cowork modes based on the complexity of your task. Along with this, Claude can now output directly into information-dense media using Docs, Slides, or Design. Deciding among all the different AI tools and their respective models can already lead to choice fatigue. If you use Claude, it may add another layer of decision-making by making you choose between Chat and Cowork. Of the two, Chat executes tasks in a simpler chatbot interface, while Cowork offloads them to an autonomous agent that can work in the background. While it’s easy to choose between the two for simpler tasks, the decision may feel overwhelming when you’re working on a more complex task that requires extensive research or analysis. To alleviate this pressure, Anthropic has decided to do away with the toggle in Claude entirely. In a blog post , the frontier lab noted that it was merging Chat and Cowork features, and Claude will be able to choose between the two on its own.

items.title: Dell may have spilled the beans on its first XPS Googlebook
items.summary: Dell might rely on the XPS brand name to position its premium Googlebook.
items.body: TL;DR Dell’s first Googlebook will be launched under the XPS name, according to a leaked document spotted online. It’s internally codenamed “Mica” and could have the model number DX13267. This corroborates an earlier Geekbench leak that pointed to the same model number. As we head toward the expected October 5 Googlebook launch , we’re steadily getting more leaks and rumors about the first wave of devices. Early last month, a Geekbench listing suggested Dell’s Googlebook might arrive under the company’s famed “XPS” name. Now, we’re getting more evidence that Dell could indeed launch its Googlebook laptops under the XPS brand. Leaker Evan Blass has shared an image of a Dell product carbon footprint disclosure document in a post on X . We were able to find the document on Dell’s website . The document clearly names the product as the “XPS Googlebook DX13267.” That model number matches the one spotted in the Geekbench listing. Blass adds that the laptop is internally codenamed “Mica.”

items.title: GrapheneOS accuses Google of gatekeeping Android 17 features and security fixes

items.body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR Google has released Android 17 QPR1 as part of the September Pixel Drop, but GrapheneOS says the update contains APIs and other changes that aren’t being made available to the wider Android ecosystem at the same time. GrapheneOS also claims Google is withholding some security fixes for standard Android components from other OEMs until Android 17 QPR2 arrives in December. Google has released the stable Android 17 QPR1 update as part of the September Pixel Drop . While the new software brings a range of features and changes to supported Pixel phones, folks over at GrapheneOS are accusing Google of gatekeeping some of the latest Android features and security fixes from other Android manufacturers and AOSP-based projects.

items.title: There’s a serious security fix hiding in Google’s September Pixel update
items.summary: Google has acknowledged that hackers may have already exploited this Pixel security vulnerability.
items.body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s September Pixel security update patches a cellular modem vulnerability that may have been used in limited, targeted attacks. CVE-2026-58704 could allow a remote attacker to bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without requiring any interaction from the victim. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Google just released the September Pixel Drop , alongside details of its monthly security fixes for Pixel devices. But amid all the new features that stable Android 17 QPR1 brings, one security flaw may have gone unnoticed. Google and other relevant authorities have now confirmed that a Pixel modem vulnerability, which has now been patched, was used in targeted exploitation.
